content:
sara: new hire can't run the python quickstart on an M1 mac. `pip install redwood-inference-sdk` fails during wheel resolution. stack trace shows it tries to build from sdist and then errors on a rust compile step.

- derek: thats because we never published macos arm64 wheels — PyPI only has manylinux x86_64 wheels. pip falls back to sdist and requires a Rust toolchain for an extension.

- li: confirmed locally: `pip debug --verbose` shows candidate distributions only for cp310-cp310-manylinux_x86_64.whl. No macosx_11_0_arm64 or universal2 wheel.

- jen: poetry users also report lockfile chaos: poetry 1.4 picks dependency ranges that conflict with our bundled `typing-extensions` constraint, ending up with incompatible extras.

- sara: any temporary suggestions I can give the new hire? they don't have rust installed on laptop and can't install system libs.

- derek: workaround: `pip install --prefer-binary redwood-inference-sdk` might pick a binary if available. Otherwise install rust via `rustup` or use `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk@main#egg=redwood-inference-sdk` which uses wheel artifacts from CI if you push them. Ugly.

- li: long term: publish macos universal2 wheels. use cibuildwheel to build both x86_64 and arm64 and produce a single universal2 wheel or two separate wheels with correct tags. GH Actions matrix should include macos-latest with runs-on: macos-13 and set `CIBW_MACOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11`.

- jen: for poetry: add `typing-extensions` to our pyproject with a permissive range (e.g., ">=4.4,<5") and mark async deps as optional extras so poetry doesn't pull `aiohttp` by default. also double-check `requires-python` supports 3.8-3.11 (we had an accidental upper bound).

- ops-bot: created ticket PKG-219: publish macos universal wheels; assigned to li.

- ci-bot: note: current wheel CI only builds manylinux2014_x86_64 and manylinux_2_17_x86_64. No macos targets. we also need to pin manylinux2014 for older linux compatibility.

- sara: could we ship a platform-tagged sdist that doesn't require Rust at build time? e.g., include prebuilt extension or move optional compiled bits behind a pure-python shim?

- derek: two options: (1) eliminate the native extension (refactor to pure python where feasible), or (2) vendor prebuilt wheel artifacts into the sdist which is frowned upon. Better to provide wheels and keep sdist as fallback.

- li: i'll add an action step using `cibuildwheel --platform macos --output-dir dist/wheels` and then `twine upload dist/wheels/*` in the release job. Will also test installation on a runner using `pip install dist/wheels/*.whl`.

- jen: i'll prepare a microrelease that: relaxes typing-extensions, adds `[project.optional-dependencies] async = ["aiohttp>=3.8"]`, and fixes `requires-python = ">=3.8"`. Also update README to show `pip install redwood-inference-sdk[async]` for async users.

- sara: thanks. i'll update onboarding doc to include `pip install --prefer-binary redwood-inference-sdk` as an interim note and a troubleshooting snippet for macs.

- derek: also add a CI smoke test in sample-app: on ubuntu and macos runners run `pip install --no-build-isolation --prefer-binary redwood-inference-sdk` and `python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)"` so we catch packaging regressions early.

- ci-bot: added sample-app workflow job `packaging-smoke` that runs on macos-latest and ubuntu-latest.

- ops-bot: PR #501 opened: add cibuildwheel macos matrix + upload step.

- li: one edge-case: Apple Silicon users sometimes use rosetta/python x86_64 which can install our manylinux wheel under certain conditions. need to ensure our tags don't accidentally break those installs. Will document the recommended approach: native arm64 wheel first, fallback to universal2, then x86_64 under rosetta.

- jen: also check wheel name patterns. cibuildwheel should produce `redwood_inference_sdk-*.macosx_11_0_universal2.whl` or `macosx_11_0_arm64.whl`. ensure our upload step doesn't drop the platform tags.

- sara: ok assigning: jen -> deps bump + pyproject; li -> CI + wheels; derek -> sample-app smoke test + docs snippet. i'll monitor PKG-219 and mark onboarding doc blocked -> in-progress.

- li: once wheels are available i'll validate by creating a fresh venv on an m1 runner and `pip install dist/wheels/*.whl`. will post results here.

- derek: also add an entry to release notes explaining the change and calling out that older versions might require rust and thus fail on stock macs.

- sara: perfect. will follow up when PRs merge. thanks everyone :+1:
